rationale: This is a one-atom ablation of the archived KnowledgeRichCapitalRestraintWithMarginRepair (only the gate's 3-year lag differs) and sits strictly between two already-tested signals, so it is a cosmetic attribution variant rather than a new economic hypothesis.

The complementary half of the same ablation exercise — it is MaturedResearchPayoffWithCapitalRestraint with the lag removed, using only legs and gates that already appear in the archive, and its own reasoning admits it exists purely to decompose an existing winner.

Replacing a single lagged R&D vintage with a cumulative knowledge stock is an economically motivated (stock-versus-flow) change rather than pure ablation, though it remains a close derivative of the archive winner and the hypothesis text ("three to five years ago") mislabels the window the expression actually computes (t-2 through t-4).

Combining the signed contrast with the lagged gate is coherent and the mechanics match the hypothesis (knowledge-poor firms collapse to the middle rather than the short tail), but it is an explicit recombination of two archived constructions and its incremental information over them is likely small.

This is close to a rediscovery of the archived SignedNetCommitmentAmplifiedByKnowledgePoverty (signed commitment contrast times industry-ranked knowledge poverty, fmb -4.12), and it is also nearly a linear combination of the raw signed contrast and Signal 4, so it adds little independent evidence on the asymmetry question.

The gate double-counts goodwill (Compustat `intan` already includes `gdwl`), and the proposal explicitly predicts a weak effect while declaring a positive expected sign, making it a placebo test that cannot satisfy the alpha/t-stat objective as constructed.
